title: NCEP R2 upward surface radiation records the 2020 and 2022 ocean temperature shifts at 60S-60N
abstract: We tested whether cold ocean temperature shifts in NCEP R2 enter its archived upward longwave radiation. We used monthly skin temperature, upward and downward flux, and ERSSTv5 on a fixed open-ocean mask at 60S-60N. A date search with no supplied event dates selects February 2020 and December 2022 in both skin-temperature error and radiation-derived temperature error. A fixed-date regression gives late levels of -0.342 K and -0.344 K. Upward flux changes by -1.986 W/m2 relative to reference emission; skin temperature predicts -1.976 W/m2. Their residual level is -0.010 W/m2, with a conditional 95 percent interval of -0.043 to +0.022. Six fit choices give reference-relative emission changes of -2.108 to -1.986 W/m2. Downward radiation falls too, so net longwave heat gain is only +0.614 W/m2 in the main fit. A small residual change in 2017 remains unexplained. This physical audit argues against a fault confined to the temperature archive. Radiation and temperature share a model, so this is not independent proof of true SST or net heat-flux error. We provide code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and retrieval instructions.

display.caption: Skin and radiation temperatures show the same reference-relative shifts. Upward flux follows skin emission while their residual changes little at the main transitions. Curves are centered 12-month means relative to 2010-2019.
